proposal.name: Close the remaining comparison review gaps

issue_plan.name: Close the remaining comparison review gaps
issue_plan.summary: Five ordered plumbing changes finish #667: move drafting authority out of command arguments, reuse checked baselines with an actionable fixed-view refusal, consolidate comparison rules and storage, preserve healthy final charts while checking receipt comparisons both ways, and share an efficient dashboard cache. They repair both weak regression cases and update SPEC.md and the linked statechart/dashboard documentation; the README overview remains accurate. The merger must record the transport, storage, validation and cache refinements, including @gitdek's chosen F1-B, because plumbing builds cannot write decisions/.

issues.title: Move captured drafting authority out of process arguments
issues.body:
Kind: plumbing

#667 found that formalization puts its baseline model, includes, view and lock into -draft-context, then the backend quotes it again inside one MCP configuration argument. Larger models can exceed Linux's 128 KiB per-argument limit. Replace that transport while preserving caller authority for modeled drafting, answers, revisions and parent-plan checks.

Keep a detached immutable CheckContext in a run-scoped caller-owned local service, outside the drafting workspace. Give the launched MCP checker only a short endpoint, a fresh run credential and the expected context digest; fetch the exact context before constructing its check tool and verify the digest and parent plan. The service only returns its captured bytes and exposes no operation for replacing them. It lives through provider retries and checker restarts within that formalization, and closes on success, setup failure and cancellation. Respect cancellation and bounded startup time when fetching; malformed, incomplete, unavailable or mismatched authority must fail the launch, never become an empty context. Preserve no-context standalone checks. Do not relocate the JSON into an environment variable, another quoted argument or a writable context file.

Direct Check calls and the independent final check still use their detached caller-memory copy. check-context.json, baseline/, previous/, proposal.json and reader.json remain guidance or proposed output, never authority. Retain the existing no-network and file-access restrictions on agent tools; the trusted MCP process can contact the caller, as it already does for tool allowances. This addresses the Linux argument limit without implementing D-0139's otherwise conditional OrbStack migration. Both supported agent backends must launch it correctly.

Inspect internal/formalize/agent.go and previews.go, cmd/invariant/main.go, internal/synth/codex.go and claudecode.go, and the allowance service in internal/synth/provider.go. Update the launch-inspecting fixtures in internal/formalize/comparison_648_accept_test.go and preview_authority_regression_test.go: they currently decode JSON following -draft-context, so the transport expectation intentionally changes while the authority assertions stay. Preserve the parent-plan checks in internal/formalize/step_depth_560_accept_test.go and cmd/invariant/preview_639_accept_test.go. The argument-recording stand-in in internal/synth/codex_test.go and Claude Code argument tests in internal/synth/synth_test.go must continue checking the actual generated configuration, permissions and tool names.

Add offline regressions that transfer a context exceeding 128 KiB, including quotes, backslashes, Unicode, includes and a large view, through a real checker child process or the normal launch path. Assert exact recovered bytes and bounded MCP configuration arguments for both backends. Exercise authorized versus invented revisions, workspace tampering, a substituted response, wrong run/digest/parent, service failure, cancellation, concurrent independent runs and cleanup. Keep coverage proving that final validation ignores derived files and uses the original authority. Tests need only local IPC, without agent accounts or Docker.

This rests on D-0014, D-0138, D-0139, D-0193, D-0355 and D-0362. Update SPEC.md's caller-context contract and docs/statecharts.md, which currently says the MCP checker receives authority in launch arguments. Cite the supporting recorded decisions in every changed SPEC bullet. The merger records the transport refinement through the decision command; do not edit decisions/ or invent a decision ID.

issues.title: Reuse checked baselines and explain fixed-view failures
issues.body:
Kind: plumbing

#667 found repeated baseline model gates and impossible repair instructions for fixed captured views. Fix baseline checking using the preceding issue's context transport, preserving D-0362's model, include, lock and view authority.

Implement @gitdek's F1-B from https://github.com/gitdek/invariant/issues/667#issuecomment-6693769970. A nonempty captured amendment view stays fixed. If its reader checks fail, refuse the amendment with the original refusal cause and a diagnostic naming the project's saved .invariant/view.json: repair that saved view in a separate change, then open a new amendment issue so it captures the corrected project. Explain that revising the existing amendment retains its baseline and cannot pick up a view-only fix. Do not suggest editing baseline/view.json in this case. When the captured view is missing, continue taking baseline/view.json from drafting, checking it at the captured model's original bounds, and explaining how to repair that supplied view. Use this distinction in the prompt, tool feedback and final diagnostic.

Within each checker session, memoize only successful complete baseline checks by exact model, include names and bytes, effective view, full captured lock and relevant pinned tool/configuration identity. Retain detached chart/too_large evidence; agent-written readers and proposal hashes alone cannot supply it. Candidate edits still rerun all applicable candidate checks and rebuild the comparison against that checked baseline. A changed drafting-supplied legacy view gets a fresh baseline check. Failed, canceled or incomplete checks are retried; a cache hit must honor cancellation and must not expose shared mutable snapshots. Bound the cache to the session and release it when the session ends. The independent final check starts with fresh baseline validation from caller-owned sources; it cannot trust the drafting check's cache or artifacts.

Repair the two weak tests in this same change. In internal/formalize/comparison_repair_test.go, retain the failed-draft recovery coverage but also construct otherwise valid ordinary reader evidence with a missing or stale required comparison, so 'failed comparison remained publishable' reaches comparison validation and asserts its specific refusal. In TestComparison648LegacyBaselineRepairAndAuthority in internal/formalize/comparison_648_accept_test.go, remove the tampered-old-files escape that accepts any problem containing 'baseline'. With a valid supplied legacy view, both the tool and final check must succeed despite edits to staged old model/lock files, and their comparison must contain the original captured sources and bounds. Assert the specific missing/invalid view failures too.

Inspect internal/formalize/comparison.go, previews.go, formalize.go, agent.go, prompt.go and cmd/invariant/main.go; their comparison_authority_test.go, reader_603_accept_test.go and preview_authority_regression_test.go fixtures; and the factory comparison flow/answer regressions. The reader603 Docker double runs the actual model/reader pipeline: it checks tlc2.TLC, --network none, -workers 1, -config, -dump dot,actionlabels, model/include bytes and original constants, and records calls. Reuse that evidence to count baseline model-gate, graph and replay work separately from candidate work; do not replace it with a precomputed chart.

Add tests proving repeated passing drafting checks run one baseline gate per unchanged key, candidate checks still run each time, changed legacy views and tool inputs invalidate reuse, failed attempts can recover, concurrent calls do not alias evidence, and a final check performs fresh baseline work. Cover nonempty malformed and hiding-invalid captured views, ignored staged replacements, a saved/reloaded amendment after a view-only branch fix, and a new amendment capturing the corrected view. Preserve 500-state limitations, faithful bounds, valid-view behavior and the existing baseline reset after another ratification or a different project.

D-0343, D-0345, D-0355 and D-0362 govern this behavior; D-0122 and D-0294 require current documentation. Update SPEC.md and docs/statecharts.md to distinguish missing-view repair from fixed-view refusal and describe session reuse versus independent final validation. The merger records F1-B and the cache refinement, including the owner's comment. Run the targeted Go suites and the pinned-TLC comparison integration command documented in docs/statecharts.md when available; unavailable Docker checks and decision recording are Merger work, while applicable real Python and TLAPS CI suites remain required.

issues.title: Consolidate comparison rules and store derived evidence once
issues.body:
Kind: plumbing

Finish #667's duplicated rules and data costs: repeated Compare calls in ValidateReader, divergent qualifications, duplicated include-name predicates, a full comparison in both .invariant/reader.json and comparison.json, and three copies of derived evidence in previous/. Preserve comparison meaning and authority.

Have one comparison-validation operation establish canonical snapshots, deltas, qualifications and fingerprint integrity. Within a Proposal.ValidateReader call, recompute the comparison once and use the validated snapshots to check the current candidate, Target.baseline and comparison_baseline. Standalone public validation boundaries, including ValidateComparisonContext, must still validate their own input; do not cache a 'valid' flag on mutable proposal/comparison objects or skip validation after a mutation. Retain source-pin, full-lock, view, bounds, chart/limitation, duplicate occurrence and candidate/required-baseline checks, including both baseline requirements if both are present. Keep canonical comparison bytes and fingerprints unchanged for the same evidence.

Use one statechart qualification helper for check feedback, comparison Markdown/SVG, receipts and dashboard messages. It must consistently state that equal charts do not establish behavioral equivalence, that the comparison is bounded and view-qualified and adds no proof claim, when view or model/include sources changed, when bounds describe different displayed scopes, and when a side is too large. Preserve per-surface source names, exact identities, bounds, legends and literal escaping. Replace the include-name predicates with one shared TLA sibling-name rule used by drafting, baseline checking and retained comparison validation: an ASCII identifier followed by .tla, with no path components and distinct from the main module. Keep regular-file/symbolic-link/hard-link checks at the I/O boundaries.

Keep in-memory proposals, formalization.json, factory markers, receipts and receipt reader.json companions self-contained. For a ratified project's .invariant files, write the full comparison only to comparison.json; reader.json contains its ordinary chart/limitation and a versioned, fingerprint-bound reference to that sibling instead of another full comparison. Current.ReadReader must load and validate the reference, reconstruct the existing in-memory Reader and preserve its existing fingerprint. Read older inline records too, requiring agreement when both inline and sibling comparisons exist. Missing, malformed or mismatched referenced evidence must produce an explicit error, never silently discard a required comparison or choose a different copy. Preserve optional readers for legacy projects and stale-file removal when writing a project without a comparison.

Stage a previous draft's complete derived evidence only in previous/proposal.json. Continue staging its editable model, sibling includes and view separately, but stop creating redundant previous/reader.json and previous/comparison.json. This intentionally changes the staging expectation in internal/formalize/reader_603_accept_test.go; move that assertion to the complete proposal record instead of dropping the evidence assertion. Point drafting guidance to that record. Revisions, partial answers, amendments, recovery and publication must retain every source and derived record, and no staged record gains checking authority.

Inspect internal/formalize/reader.go, comparison.go, agent.go and prompt.go; internal/statechart/comparison.go and its Markdown/SVG consumers; internal/verify/reader_comparison.go; and internal/dashboard/comparisons.go and reader.go. Existing tests to retain or deliberately update include internal/formalize/reader_603_accept_test.go, reader_persistence_regression_test.go, comparison_648_accept_test.go and the repaired comparison_repair_test.go; internal/statechart/comparison_648_accept_test.go and comparison_regression_test.go; internal/factory/comparison_648_accept_test.go; internal/verify/comparison_648_accept_test.go; and internal/dashboard/comparison_648_accept_test.go. Read shared fixtures before naming allowed test files.

Add mutation tests proving every comparison field and candidate/baseline binding still refuses damage after the validation consolidation, and focused instrumentation or benchmarks demonstrating the removed repeated work. Test identical qualification content across publishers for unchanged/view-changed/model-changed/different-bound/limited comparisons, with literal hostile and Unicode text. Test the common include rule on valid underscore names, main-module collisions, absolute/relative paths, separators and malformed suffixes. Test new reference-based persistence, historical inline loading, missing/wrong sibling evidence, nonmutating round trips, legacy readers, stale cleanup and single-copy previous staging. Preserve existing proposal hashes, ratified locks, verification fingerprints and saved comparison fingerprints.

This rests on D-0345, D-0351, D-0355 and D-0362. Update SPEC.md and docs/statecharts.md for the on-disk reference and previous-draft layout, validation and shared qualifications, with recorded decision citations. The merger records the new storage/validation policy; the build cannot write decisions/. Run affected Go package tests and relevant persistence, recovery and receipt tests, with the documented pinned-TLC integration check as Merger work if Docker is unavailable.

issues.title: Check receipt comparisons both ways and retain healthy final charts
issues.body:
Kind: plumbing

Fix #667's two dashboard evidence bugs: omitted receipt comparisons escape checking, and damaged comparisons suppress healthy final charts. Use the preceding issue's shared comparison validation and wording.

Recompute the expected comparison outcome from the receipt commit's captured .invariant/comparison.json through the same validation used by verification, regardless of whether the receipt has a Comparison field. Compare both sides' presence and complete outcome: no file means no retained comparison; a valid file requires the matching full comparison and candidate lock identity; damaged or undrawable evidence requires a comparison diagnostic. Do not treat an absent receipt comparison as authority to skip the file, and do not infer an empty graph from absent evidence. Use this symmetric recomputation rather than adding another input-hash schema. Preserve legacy receipts from commits with no comparison and the intentional distinction between proposal candidate sources and a separately synthesized final model.

Validate the final-model reader independently of comparison validation. A failure confined to the comparison becomes a visible printable comparison_evidence diagnostic and removes only the comparison presentation. When the receipt's final chart is independently sound, keep it on the card, its poster where applicable, the evidence page and the native SVG beside the diagnostic. Continue checking the receipt commit's model/includes/view/lock, report and reader fingerprints, pins, bounds, tools, counts, chart consistency and companion evidence. Do not rescue unrelated corrupt or missing final evidence, accept an arbitrary archived image, or mutate the retained report to make a fingerprint pass. Separate comparison-only presentation differences from final-chart companion mismatches so fallback cannot bypass those checks. For a final limitation or unavailable reader, keep that specific outcome alongside the comparison diagnostic instead of claiming a chart.

Render validated final evidence with the shared native renderer, distinguish it from proposal evidence, and bind diagnostics, sources and rendered content into immutable URLs/ETags. Never serve a forged comparison image at a formerly valid URL. Apply the same behavior to public cards and /act. Disk cache corruption still follows D-0353's whole-snapshot refusal and recovery policy; a legitimately recorded comparison diagnostic is not permission to accept a damaged cache.

The affected paths are internal/verify/reader_comparison.go and reader.go, internal/dashboard/reader.go and dashboard.go, and the receipt renderer if needed to share safe diagnostic presentation. Inspect internal/dashboard/comparison_648_accept_test.go, comparison_identity_regression_test.go, reader_631_accept_test.go, reader_recovery_regression_test.go, reader_missing_archive_regression_test.go and reader_regression_test.go, plus internal/verify/comparison_648_accept_test.go and comparison_render_regression_test.go and internal/receipt/reader_writer_regression_test.go. These fixtures build complete bound reports/archives and fake GitHub reads at one commit. Keep unrelated bindings valid so each tamper case reaches its intended comparison check.

Test valid comparison presence, omitted receipt comparison despite a valid commit file, unexpected receipt comparison without a file, malformed/stale/undrawable comparison and diagnostic mismatch, and a different valid comparison at the commit. In each damaged-comparison case start with demonstrably valid final evidence and assert its full topology survives beside the specific diagnostic on card/page/SVG and across a restart. Independently corrupt the final chart, its source binding, reader.json and native SVG and require refusal. Cover no-comparison legacy behavior, differently synthesized final sources, too_large and unavailable final outcomes, safe literal diagnostics, changed presentation identity and conditional HTTP responses. Preserve no-comparison identities where the evidence and rendered output are unchanged.

D-0351, D-0353, D-0362 and D-0364 govern the reader, comparison and poster boundaries. Update SPEC.md, docs/statecharts.md and docs/dashboard.md to describe symmetric binding and comparison-only fallback; every changed SPEC bullet cites its recorded grounds. The merger records this refinement. Verification verdicts, assurance, verification fingerprints, proposal hashes and locks remain unaffected. Run affected Go tests, archive/restart regressions and the normal required checks; decision recording and unavailable local Docker/network checks are Merger work, not replacements for applicable real Python or TLAPS CI.

issues.title: Share and bound dashboard proposal evidence caching
issues.body:
Kind: plumbing

Finish #667 with a shared proposal/preview cache: refreshes currently revalidate, render and write every comparison, restore builds each page twice, and superseded pages accumulate. Preserve the two evidence types' validation, rendering and damage policies.

Key reuse by the complete detached input evidence and presentation/validation format, including repository and issue, option identity and words where applicable, all sources, choices, reader/comparison contents and diagnostics. A proposal hash, retained fingerprint field, pointer identity or issue number alone is insufficient. Unchanged evidence in the same server must reuse its already validated page and presentation without invoking comparison/preview validation, SVG generation or a disk write again. Changed source, evidence, enclosing words, diagnostics or renderer contract must miss and produce its own presentation. Keep published page identities bound to both structured evidence and rendered bytes; the lookup key is not authority for an unvalidated record.

Share input lookup, atomic persistence, installation, restoration and eviction between comparisons.go and previews.go, with their own typed evidence validators and renderers. On cold restore, validate the saved structured record and its expected presentation, build it once, then install that exact result without a second render or rewriting an unchanged file. A missing/corrupt/mismatched entry produces the existing visible diagnostic for only its proposal or option, preserving healthy siblings. Entries whose proposal is absent lose dangling links as before. Persistence failures stay retryable and must not mark an unwritten entry durably saved.

After a successful replacement snapshot is published, evict superseded proposal/preview pages and their persisted evidence that no current served snapshot references. Do not prune during a failed refresh or before replacing the old snapshot; keep pages referenced by any current repository, healthy sibling, or receipt. Apply the same reachability cleanup after a successful restart restoration, so old entries do not accumulate across runs. Coordinate publication, eviction and concurrent HTTP access: a served snapshot never points to an evicted current page, and an evicted immutable URL can return not found but must never serve different contents. Preserve receipt archive retry and whole-snapshot recovery rules; this cache refactor does not broaden the receipt salvage policy from the preceding change.

Inspect internal/dashboard/comparisons.go, previews.go, reader.go and dashboard.go, with preview_cache_regression_test.go, preview_639_accept_test.go, comparison_648_accept_test.go, comparison_identity_regression_test.go, reader_recovery_regression_test.go and reader_missing_archive_regression_test.go and their snapshot/HTTP fixtures. Keep source-snapshot trust and factory marker-author checks unchanged. A renderer/validation format change must invalidate old entries deliberately, with the existing diagnostic/recovery behavior.

Add deterministic counter-based regressions showing many identical refreshes validate/render/persist each proposal or preview once; healthy cold restore builds once and performs no redundant write; changed evidence invalidates reuse even with the same statement hash; missing/corrupt evidence isolates damage; and failed persistence is retried. Publish revisions, removed waiting items and multiple repositories to prove old proposal/preview memory and disk entries are reclaimed while every live page and healthy sibling remains available. Cover failed-refresh retention, restart cleanup, concurrent reads/builds and changed formats, with race-detector runs where available. Preserve identical bytes, URLs and ETags for unchanged valid presentations under the same format, and retain native script-free SVG and literal text.

This rests on D-0353, D-0355, D-0362 and D-0368. Update SPEC.md and docs/dashboard.md for shared reuse, one-pass restoration and the superseded-page retention policy, and docs/statecharts.md where it describes immutable proposal/preview recovery. Cite recorded decisions; the merger records the cache refinement through the decision command. Run the dashboard suites and affected rendering tests. This completes the planned #667 work.
